title: Construct Target Array With Multiple Sums
summary: Given an array target with n integers, determine if it can be constructed from an initial array arr of n ones by repeatedly setting an element to the sum of all elements in arr.
statement: Given an array target with n integers, determine if it can be constructed from an initial array arr of n ones by repeatedly setting an element to the sum of all elements in arr.
constraints: Begin with an array of ones.
A move replaces one element by the current total sum while leaving all others unchanged.
Return whether the positive target array can be constructed.
reference_solution:
def can_construct_target_array(target):
    import heapq
    if len(target)==1:return target[0]==1
    total=sum(target);heap=[-value for value in target];heapq.heapify(heap)
    while True:
        maximum=-heapq.heappop(heap);rest=total-maximum
        if maximum==1 or rest==1:return True
        if rest==0 or maximum<=rest or maximum%rest==0:return False
        previous=maximum%rest;total=rest+previous;heapq.heappush(heap,-previous)
hints: Reverse the last move, which must have created the current largest value.
The other values sum to rest; the prior largest value is maximum modulo rest after skipping repeated reverse subtractions.
Use a max-heap, and handle rest equal to one as immediately reachable.
The largest value uniquely identifies the last changed position, so each reverse step is necessary and preserves equivalence.
editorial: Reverse the operation: if maximum was last replaced, its previous value differs by a positive multiple of the sum of all other entries. Modulo performs all repeated subtractions at once. Reject nonpositive predecessors and accept when all values reduce to one or the remainder sum is one. The oracle independently explores every bounded forward state on seeded small targets.

tests.explanation: Reversing the largest values recovers [1,1,1], so the target is constructible.
No forward replacement from all ones can create this target.
